info.title: topwater
info.description: The topwater command: a simulated bash shell in your terminal, one-shot runs, snapshots, and an MCP server that gives any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) a sandboxed bash tool.

commands.name: FILE
commands.description: write the machine (and its history, if it has one) to FILE as a .topwater file

options.name: --state
options.description: load the machine from FILE if it exists; save it there after every command and on exit

options.name: --from
options.description: start from the snapshot FILE when there is no --state file yet (FILE is never written)

options.name: --import
options.description: copy the host file or directory HOST into the machine at PATH when it starts (a copy, never live)

options.name: --export
options.description: copy PATH out of the machine to the host path HOST when it exits

options.name: --timeout
options.description: time limit for one command (default 120)

options.name: --disk
options.description: size of the simulated disk (default 128)

commands.name: FILE
commands.description: check FILE and make its machine the --state file

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: serve the machine over stdio as an MCP server with one `bash` tool

commands.name: FILE
commands.description: re-run a recorded session and report every call that prints something else

commands.name: run
commands.description: run one command, print its output, exit with its exit code

commands.name: shell
commands.description: an interactive shell on the simulated machine (the default)

commands.name: snapshot
commands.description: write the machine to FILE, open a shell on FILE, or describe FILE
